steps.body: The same rule rounds to any place, not just wholes. Pick your target place, then look at the digit **one place to its right** — the *decider*. To round to the nearest tenth, look at the hundredths digit: 5 or more rounds the tenths up, 4 or less leaves it. So 3.16 rounds to 3.2.

widget.prompt: Place 2.46. Then ask which TENTH mark it is nearest.
widget.successFeedback: 2.46 sits between 2.4 and 2.5, and past their midpoint of 2.45 — so it rounds to 2.5. Rounding to a place means choosing the nearest mark at THAT place, and the line shows which one it is.

predict.prompt: Before you place it: is 2.46 closer to 2 or to 3?
predict.reveal: 2.46 sits 0.46 from 2 and 0.54 from 3 — the 2 side wins. Halfway would be 2.50, and 0.46 falls short of 0.50 — only the part after the point decides which whole number is nearer. Judging position from the endpoints first makes the exact placement easier to defend.

steps.body: To round to the nearest **hundredth**, the target moves one place right — so the decider does too, becoming the **thousandths** digit. Look there: 5 or more rounds the hundredths up. The rule never changes; only which place you target and which you check.

steps.body: Target a place; check the one to its right.
takeaways: To round to any place, look at the digit one place to its right — the decider.
5 or more rounds the target place up; 4 or less leaves it.
Nearest tenth checks hundredths; nearest hundredth checks thousandths.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **To round to a place, check the digit just to its right.** For the nearest tenth, look at the hundredths digit: 5 or more rounds the tenths up, 4 or less keeps it. So 0.63 → 0.6 (the 3 is under 5) and 0.68 → 0.7 (the 8 is 5+).
